workload.title: W2b with a shorter preemption quantum
workload.note: W5 found most of a short request's remaining wait outside the runqueue: its packet waits on a core busy with a 50 us handler that is never preempted (quantum 100 us). The IOKernel preempts a thread that ran past runtime_quantum_us while its core has pending work (checked every 10 us). Prediction: with q10, prio's short wait at rho 0.9 drops well below 18 us; long requests pay for the preemptions.

calibration.iters_per_us_note: loadgen --calibrate 100 --fakework sqrt on the server node under the runtime: 32674, 32717, 32672 iterations per 100 us
calibration.overhead_us_note: per-request cost beyond the handler's work: 10 us requests on 4 kthreads saturate at 393k req/s (results/probe-10us), 4 / 393k = 10.2 us
calibration.testbed_note: server and client on one node (hp070), IOKernel 'ias noht' with loopback: control core 0, dataplane core 1, server and client kthreads on cores 2-9 with no shared hyperthreads
